R29.2.not_verifiable: Player behaviour: level 3 (reference-player). Whether a capability parameter is sent is the Player's choice, and a slot parameter is due only when the slot declares it, which needs the window the request was built from
R29.2.quote: - **R29.2** (Player): Sending a capability parameter is OPTIONAL. A Player conformant to this specification MAY send all of them, some of them, or none. A slot parameter is sent when the slot declares its value, as R38.2, R39.3 and R41.5 require, and not otherwise.

R29.3.quote: - **R29.3** (Player): When the Player has no value for a reserved parameter, or does not disclose its value, the Player MUST omit that parameter entirely rather than send it with an empty or placeholder value.

R29.4.not_verifiable: Player behaviour: level 3 (reference-player). A request does not show which parameters the Player added and which came with the Publisher's event URL (R18.2), and only the first need the vendor prefix
R29.4.quote: - **R29.4** (Player): A parameter that is not one of the reserved names MUST carry a vendor-specific prefix, so that reserved names added in a later edition cannot collide with it.

R29.5.not_verifiable: how an APS behaves on receiving a request without a parameter; no document records it
R29.5.quote: - **R29.5** (APS): The APS MUST tolerate the absence of any reserved parameter and MUST be able to produce ad candidates without receiving any of them. An APS that requires a parameter in order to answer would make R29.2 unattainable for the Player.

R29.7.not_verifiable: an absent capability parameter is legal; its meaning (undetermined) binds the APS's resolution, which no document records
R29.7.quote: - **R29.7** (spec document): A capability parameter absent from the resolution request means its value is **undetermined** — the Player did not determine it, or did not disclose it. Absence does NOT assert that the device lacks the capability. This specification does not define how an APS resolves an undetermined value; that is the APS's decision, and two APSs that resolve it differently are both conformant. *Informative note:* an APS that does not know a capability can return every option the advertiser allowed and leave the choice to the Player's check (R5.6), which keeps every device that could render one of them.

R3.1.not_verifiable: the class is derived and never sent: a reserved-looking name for it fails R29.1a, and a vendor-named one cannot be recognised by code; giving each class its behaviour is a property of the specification's prose (what it states, cites or justifies), not of a document instance; judged by validate-spec
R3.1.quote: - **R3.1** (spec document): A device class is a named combination of the first three capability parameters of R29.1, so the parameters tell every class apart by construction. The classes are the rows of this table, and this table is their only definition: | Class | `sgai-video-decoders` | `sgai-image-over-video` | `sgai-html-over-video` | |---|---|---|---| | D1 — top tier | `2` or `3` | `1` | `1` | | D2 | `2` | `0` | `0` | | D3 | `1` | `1` | `1` | | D4 | `1` | `1` | `0` | | D5 — worst case | `1` | `0` | `0` | No two rows overlap. A device whose combination is not in the table (two decoders with image and without HTML, for example) belongs to no named class; it declares its parameters the same way, and its behaviour follows from them as for any other. The specification MUST give, for each class, the expected behaviour for each ad opportunity type covered by the use cases.

R3.2.quote: - **R3.2** (Player): A Player on any supported device class MUST produce a defined behaviour (render, fall back, or skip) for every ad opportunity type defined in the spec; undefined behaviour is non-conforming.

R30.1.not_verifiable: that the empty resolution is a complete, well-formed document is the schema's (level 1); that it is not an error status or an empty body is a property of the HTTP response, which no example carries
R30.1.quote: - **R30.1** (APS): An opportunity that resolved with no ads MUST be expressed as a resolution document carrying no candidates, and MUST NOT be expressed as an error response or as a response without a body.

R30.2.quote: - **R30.2** (Player): A resolution carrying no candidates MUST NOT count as an execution of the opportunity. Where the opportunity's event carries `@executeOnce="true"`, the event remains executable afterwards, per §5.16.2.2.2 and §5.16.2.2.6 NOTE 3.

R31.1.quote: - **R31.1** (spec document): A viewer pause that begins inside a pause opportunity window MUST trigger a resolution request for that window, and a pause that begins outside every such window MUST NOT trigger one.

R31.2a.not_verifiable: the Publisher part forbids an interpretation, not a value: any declared cap on a pause window is legal
R31.2a.quote: - **R31.2** (Publisher + Player): The Publisher-declared slot cap (R4) MUST NOT be interpreted as bounding the duration of a pause slot. R4's cap bounds an end on a replacement slot and a cumulative duration elsewhere; on a pause slot it bounds neither, because there is no authored duration for it to bound.

R31.2b.quote: - **R31.2** (Publisher + Player): The Publisher-declared slot cap (R4) MUST NOT be interpreted as bounding the duration of a pause slot. R4's cap bounds an end on a replacement slot and a cumulative duration elsewhere; on a pause slot it bounds neither, because there is no authored duration for it to bound.

R32.1a.quote: - **R32.1** (APS): A resolution document for a pause slot MUST declare which of three behaviours applies once its candidates are exhausted while the viewer is still paused: - **`repeat`** — the sequence is presented again from the start, for as long as the pause lasts; - **`request-again`** — a new resolution document is requested for the same pause; - **`stop`** — no further ad is presented; the paused primary frame is shown. A document that declares none means `stop`, and `stop` MUST then apply.

R32.1b.not_verifiable: what repeat, request-again and stop mean, and the default, bind the Player (level 3)
R32.1b.quote: - **R32.1** (APS): A resolution document for a pause slot MUST declare which of three behaviours applies once its candidates are exhausted while the viewer is still paused: - **`repeat`** — the sequence is presented again from the start, for as long as the pause lasts; - **`request-again`** — a new resolution document is requested for the same pause; - **`stop`** — no further ad is presented; the paused primary frame is shown. A document that declares none means `stop`, and `stop` MUST then apply.

R32.2.quote: - **R32.2** (Player): Under `request-again`, a resolution document carrying no candidates (R30) MUST be treated as `stop` for the remainder of that pause.

R32.4.not_verifiable: a property of the specification's prose (what it states, cites or justifies), not of a document instance; judged by validate-spec
R32.4.quote: - **R32.4** (spec document): Whether a second resolution request within one pause is the same opportunity or a new one is **out of scope**. The two readings are identical at the Player: it requests, it renders what arrives, and it stops on resume, in both. What differs is accounting between the APS and the ADS, which this specification does not observe (R18), so it is in no position to fix which reading is correct. What the specification does measure is **how much of the paused interval carried an ad** (R33), and that figure is the same however the requests are counted.

R33.1.not_verifiable: a property of the specification's prose (what it states, cites or justifies), not of a document instance; judged by validate-spec
R33.1.quote: - **R33.1** (spec document): This specification MUST NOT define a metric of its own for pause-ad delivery. The quantity is derived from the `PlayList` metric of Annex D.4.6; defining a parallel metric for something the base specification already measures is the duplication R9 exists to prevent.

R33.2.quote: - **R33.2** (Player): A Player that reports metrics MUST derive the paused interval from the `PlayList` entries: it is the interval between the end of a playback period whose last rendered stretch stopped on `UserRequest`, and the `start` of the next entry whose `starttype` is `Resume`. It MUST NOT count a playback period that stopped on `Rebuffering` as a pause opportunity. *Privacy note:* the `PlayList` entries record what the viewer did — when they paused, sought and resumed. Reporting metrics is optional (DP-4), and whether a Player reports them is subject to the policies that apply to whoever deploys it.

R33.3.not_verifiable: a property of the specification's prose (what it states, cites or justifies), not of a document instance; judged by validate-spec
R33.3.quote: - **R33.3** (spec document): The transport by which any measurement reaches the Publisher, the APS or the ADS is out of scope, as it is for the base specification's own metrics (§5.9.1).

R33.4.quote: - **R33.4** (Publisher): Content carrying pause opportunity windows MUST request the `PlayList` metric through the base specification's `Metrics` element, in the `MPD` that declares the windows. An alternative presentation that declares pause windows of its own (R40.6) requests the metric in its own `MPD`; the request of the presentation that triggered it does not cover it. Collection is triggered by the service provider and not by the Player — *"The trigger mechanism is based on the `Metrics` element in the MPD"* (§5.9.1) — so without this declaration R33.2 defines how to derive a quantity that nothing obliges anyone to collect.

R41.7.quote: - **R41.7** (Player): The Player MUST render at most one audio source at any instant, at the volume and mute state the viewer set on the device. This specification defines no mixing, ducking or gain level.

R42.1.not_verifiable: occurrence beacons: no carrier is bound for it: context/06 leaves the name to the build and the specification under test declares none the catalogue recognises; undecidable until one is named and bound in vocab.py
R42.1.quote: - **R42.1** (spec document): The specification MUST define a normative carrier for beacons bound to an occurrence rather than to a presentation time, for this closed set of occurrences on an accepted ad: the viewer dismisses or skips it (R35); the viewer pauses it and resumes it; the viewer mutes or unmutes it; it fails at runtime (R1.4, R1.6); none of its options renders and at least one of them failed its first request (R5.9). The set is closed for this edition. Each such beacon MUST fire once per occurrence, when the occurrence happens on the ad that carries it, and never from the timeline.

R42.2.not_verifiable: needs the occurrence carrier and what the ADS declared; no carrier is bound for it: context/06 leaves the name to the build and the specification under test declares none the catalogue recognises; undecidable until one is named and bound in vocab.py
R42.2.quote: - **R42.2** (APS): When the ADS declared beacons for any of these occurrences, the APS MUST carry them in that carrier and not in the callback scheme. Whether they reach the resolution document at all is part of the APS-to-ADS contract (R18), as in R28.3.

R42.3.quote: - **R42.3** (Player): A Player conformant to this specification MUST read the carrier of R42.1 and fire its beacons with the meaning R42.1 gives them.

R42.4.not_verifiable: a property of the specification's prose (what it states, cites or justifies), not of a document instance; judged by validate-spec
R42.4.quote: - **R42.4** (spec document): The annex that maps a VAST response to a resolution document (R11.5) MUST show which VAST tracking events map to each occurrence.

R44.1.not_verifiable: verification resources: no carrier is bound for it: context/06 leaves the name to the build and the specification under test declares none the catalogue recognises; undecidable until one is named and bound in vocab.py
R44.1.quote: - **R44.1** (spec document): The specification MUST define a carrier, per candidate, for the verification resources the ADS declared: for each, a vendor identifier, an optional resource locator and optional opaque parameters. Their meaning belongs to the vendor, not to this specification.

R44.2.not_verifiable: an obligation between parties outside the documents (the APS-to-ADS contract, R18): no document shows it; and no carrier is bound for it: context/06 leaves the name to the build and the specification under test declares none the catalogue recognises; undecidable until one is named and bound in vocab.py
R44.2.quote: - **R44.2** (APS): When the ADS declared verification resources for an ad, the APS MUST carry them in that carrier. Fidelity is part of the APS-to-ADS contract (R18).

R44.3.quote: - **R44.3** (Player): Running a verification SDK is OPTIONAL. A Player that runs one MUST hand it the verification resources and the creative identifiers (R23.2) of the candidate it renders, and the region the ad occupies on screen, which on a squeezeback is not the region of the primary content. *Privacy note:* a verification SDK measures the device and its screen, and what it measures leaves the Player for a third party. Running one is optional (DP-4), and whether a Player runs one is subject to the policies that apply to whoever deploys it.

R47.1.not_verifiable: viewability beacons ride the occurrence carrier of R42.1: no carrier is bound for it: context/06 leaves the name to the build and the specification under test declares none the catalogue recognises; undecidable until one is named and bound in vocab.py
R47.1.quote: - **R47.1** (APS): When the ADS declared viewability beacons for an ad, the APS MUST carry them in the carrier of R42.1, each marked with which of the three outcomes it reports. Fidelity is part of the APS-to-ADS contract (R18). Each beacon reports its outcome: it MUST fire once per impression when that outcome is determined, and the undetermined beacon is the outcome of a Player that does not determine viewability.

R47.2.quote: - **R47.2** (Player): A Player conformant to this specification MUST fire the beacons of R47.1 with that meaning: the beacon of the outcome it determined, or, when it does not determine it, the undetermined beacon when the candidate carries one. *Privacy note:* whether an ad was viewable is a determination the Player makes about the viewer's screen, and the beacon of a determined outcome discloses it. Determining it is optional (DP-4); the undetermined beacon discloses nothing about the device.

R47.3.not_verifiable: a property of the specification's prose (what it states, cites or justifies), not of a document instance; judged by validate-spec
R47.3.quote: - **R47.3** (spec document): The annex of R11.5 MUST show how a VAST viewability declaration maps to the three outcomes.

R48.1.not_verifiable: regulatory disclosure: no carrier is bound for it: context/06 leaves the name to the build and the specification under test declares none the catalogue recognises; undecidable until one is named and bound in vocab.py
R48.1.quote: - **R48.1** (spec document): The specification MUST define a carrier, per candidate, for the disclosure information the ADS declared for that ad: an identifier of the disclosure programme, and optionally a visual indicator, a destination URL, the name of the party on whose behalf the ad is presented and, when different, of the party that paid for it, and a short label identifying the content as advertising.

R48.2.not_verifiable: an obligation between parties outside the documents (the APS-to-ADS contract, R18): no document shows it; and no carrier is bound for it: context/06 leaves the name to the build and the specification under test declares none the catalogue recognises; undecidable until one is named and bound in vocab.py
R48.2.quote: - **R48.2** (APS): When the ADS declared disclosure information for an ad, the APS MUST carry it in that carrier. Fidelity is part of the APS-to-ADS contract (R18).

R48.3.quote: - **R48.3** (Player): When the candidate it renders carries disclosure information, the Player MUST make it available to the viewer by the means its device has. How is up to the Player: rendering the visual indicator, a device-native indicator, or a remote-control action that shows the destination URL on screen all conform. A Player MUST NOT fetch a visual indicator it cannot render, because fetching it can be counted as a view of it.

R5.1.quote: - **R5.1** (APS): Each ad candidate in the resolution document the Player reads MUST carry one or more **renderable presentation options (each a form plus its layout) as an ordered list, where document order is the preference order**. How many options a candidate carries is the APS's decision: this specification sets no maximum, and no minimum beyond one. Conformance is checked against the APS's resolution document, which is the only artefact on the path to the Player that this specification defines. A candidate MAY carry several options, each pairing a form with an admissible layout, and they form a single list. The order is the preference: the option presented MUST be the **first one, in document order,** that satisfies R5.6 and R5.9.

R5.3.quote: - **R5.3** (Player): A candidate none of whose options satisfies R5.6 and R5.9 MUST be skipped, and the Player falls through to the next candidate in document order (R7.1). When the candidates are exhausted and none was rendered, the attempt produced no ad and R20.1 governs what follows; when at least one was rendered, the Player MUST continue with the primary content.

R5.4.not_verifiable: an obligation between parties outside the documents (the APS-to-ADS contract, R18): no document shows it; it fixes what the specification may not be read as requiring
R5.4.quote: - **R5.4** (ADS + APS): This specification MUST NOT be read as obliging the ADS or the APS to maintain a device-class matrix or a per-Player capability view in order to produce candidates. An implementation that keeps one is conformant; one that does not is equally conformant.

R5.6.quote: - **R5.6** (Player): The Player MUST check each option against (a) device capabilities — it MUST NOT attempt to render an ad form (video, image, HTML) its device cannot render — and (b) the layouts the slot admits: the declared allowed layouts, or those R38.1 admits when none is declared. An option that fails either MUST NOT be rendered, and the Player moves to the next option in document order (R5.1). Forwarding the allowed layouts to the APS (R38.2) does not remove check (b).

R5.8.not_verifiable: what the options represent (the formats the advertiser allowed) is not visible in the document
R5.8.quote: - **R5.8** (spec document): The advertiser is expected to allow only the formats it wants for its ad, and the ADS that serves the ad returns only those (R2). The presentation options of a candidate are therefore the formats the advertiser allowed, and that alone restricts what the Player can choose from: the Player never renders a format that is not among the candidate's options. The options are ordered by the advertiser's preference, and the Player takes the first one its device can render (R5.6). An advertiser that wants one specific format allows only that one, and the candidate carries a single option.

R5.9.quote: - **R5.9** (Player): The first request the Player makes for each resource an option references decides whether that option is satisfiable. When that request fails — a final HTTP status outside the 2xx range, a network error, or no response within a time the Player chooses — the option is not satisfiable, and the Player MUST move to the next option in document order, as R5.6 requires for an option that fails a check. Only the first request for each resource governs this; a failure after the option has begun rendering is a runtime failure under R1.4. This specification fixes no timeout value. When no option of the candidate renders and at least one failed under this criterion, R42 governs the failure beacon.

R6.3.quote: - **R6.3** (spec document): A new tracking carrier MAY be introduced only when the callback scheme cannot express the required semantics, and only after a documented gap analysis per R9.

R6.4.quote: - **R6.4** (Player): A Player MUST safely ignore unknown namespaces on tracking-related extension elements, per the DASH extension rules invoked by R1.

R6.5.not_verifiable: any assignment of @id is legal; its scope decides which beacons fire once, which is level 3
R6.5.quote: - **R6.5** (spec document): In a non-linear resolution document, the scope of a beacon's `@id` is **the candidate** that carries it. Within a candidate, beacons sharing an `@id`, or the same URL at the same presentation time, are one beacon and fire once. Two beacons carrying the same `@id` in two different candidates of one resolution document are two distinct beacons, and both MUST fire. On a `ListMPD` the base scope applies unchanged (R1.5): `Event@id` is scoped to its `@schemeIdUri` / `@value` pair over the whole media presentation (DASH Table 44), so the ads of one `ListMPD`, streams merged from their sub-MPDs included, share one scope. The per-candidate scope above governs the candidates of a non-linear resolution document.

R6.7.not_verifiable: a property of the specification's prose (what it states, cites or justifies), not of a document instance; judged by validate-spec
R6.7.quote: - **R6.7** (spec document): The specification MUST state how a resolution document carrying the candidate-level beacon carrier is validated. A validation procedure that reports such a document valid while skipping the foreign-namespace subtree has not checked the tracking carrier at all, which is the outcome a reader is most likely to arrive at by default.

R7.1.not_verifiable: any order of candidates is legal; it binds presentation, which is level 3
R7.1.quote: - **R7.1** (spec document): The order of the candidates in a resolution document, linear and non-linear alike, is their order of presentation: they MUST be presented in that order, each starting when the previous one ends, and MUST NOT be re-ordered, deduplicated or otherwise rearranged. A candidate skipped under R5.3 is not a rearrangement and occupies no time: the next one starts where the skipped one would have started.
